docs.title: 眨眼呼叫 用户手册
docs.text:
眨眼呼叫是一款为渐冻症患者设计的辅助呼叫软件。患者按照预先设置的睁眼、闭眼动作完成眨眼序列后，电脑或蓝牙音箱会播放提醒声音，帮助患者呼叫家属或照护者。

下载最新版本 第一次使用 遇到问题

免责声明

本工具仅用于辅助看护，不能替代人工看护。请勿因使用本工具而减少或免除必要的人工看护。

适用版本

本手册适用于眨眼呼叫 v1.8.0。目前只有 Windows 版可以直接下载使用。

docs.title: 我是第一次使用
docs.text: 请按照首次使用依次完成下载、解压、模型文件下载、摄像头设置和测试呼叫。

docs.title: 我已经配置完成
docs.text: 请查看日常使用，确认每天使用前需要检查的项目，以及如何触发和停止呼叫。

docs.title: 软件没有正常工作
docs.text: 请进入遇到问题，按照页面提示检查软件、模型文件、摄像头、眨眼识别和提醒声音。

docs.title: 适合谁使用
docs.text:
• 说话困难，无法方便地发出呼叫声音。
  • 手部操作困难，无法稳定点击按钮或使用实体呼叫器。
  • 可以通过睁眼、闭眼完成简单动作。
  • 有家属或照护者协助完成首次配置和测试。

docs.title: 使用前需要准备
docs.text:
• 一台 Windows 电脑。
  • 一个能够清楚拍到患者双眼的摄像头。
  • 电脑扬声器或蓝牙音箱。
  • 首次下载模型文件时可用的网络连接。

docs.title: 下载软件
docs.text:
下面三个下载地址任选其一：

  • GitHub 最新版本
  • 百度网盘
  • 夸克网盘

下载软件压缩包后，请先将它完整解压到一个固定位置，再双击文件夹中的 BlinkCall.exe。不要直接在压缩包内运行软件。

docs.title: 正式使用前
docs.text:
请让患者和照护者共同完成至少一次测试呼叫，并确认：

  • 摄像头画面连续、清楚，患者的双眼完整可见。
  • 患者能够完成当前设置的眨眼序列。
  • 电脑或蓝牙音箱的提醒声音足够清楚。
  • 照护者知道如何停止提醒声音。

软件或使用环境发生变化后，例如更换摄像头、移动电脑或调整眨眼动作，应重新完成一次测试呼叫。

docs.title: 公益免费
docs.text: 本软件完全公益免费。

docs.title: 其他设置与技术支持
docs.text: 本页包括语言、界面显示以及排查问题时使用的录制、日志和恢复默认设置。日常呼叫一般不需要开启录制或调试模式。

docs.title: 切换语言
docs.text:
进入：

设置 → 常规 → 语言

可以选择中文或 English。点击“保存”后，软件界面会切换到所选语言。

docs.title: 切换亮色或暗色模式
docs.text:
进入：

设置 → 常规 → 亮暗模式

可以选择亮色模式或暗色模式。这个设置只改变界面外观，不影响摄像头识别和呼叫功能。

docs.title: 录制当前相机数据
docs.text:
这个功能用于保存一段当前摄像头画面，帮助开发者或工作人员排查识别问题。普通日常使用不需要开启。

进入：

设置 → 其他 → 录制当前相机数据

操作步骤：

  1. 设置最长录制时长。
  2. 选择本地电脑文件夹。
  3. 点击“开始录制”。
  4. 软件返回主界面并开始录制。
  5. 需要提前结束时，点击主界面上的停止录制按钮。

保护患者隐私

摄像头录制可能包含患者面部和周围环境。录制和分享前应征得患者或监护人同意。不要把包含敏感画面的文件直接上传到公开的 GitHub 问题中。

docs.title: 开启调试模式和日志
docs.text:
调试模式用于显示软件运行信息。工作人员需要查看识别状态或排查异常时再开启。

进入：

设置 → 其他 → 调试模式

如果需要将日志保存为文件：

  1. 开启“调试模式”。
  2. 将“是否保存至本地”设为“是”。
  3. 选择本地日志目录。
  4. 点击“保存”并重新操作，直到问题再次出现。

调试模式开启后，所选目录还会生成单独的 audio_status.log。它记录音频输出设备变更、铃声文件和音量、加载/播放状态、播放请求和停止事件，可用于排查“已触发呼叫但没有声音”的问题。该文件会滚动保存，保留最近的几份记录。

问题排查结束后，可以关闭调试模式，避免主界面持续显示技术信息。

docs.title: 恢复默认设置
docs.text:
如果动作、摄像头、声音或界面设置被改乱，可以进入：

设置 → 其他 → 恢复默认设置

确认后，软件会恢复默认配置并关闭设置窗口。

恢复默认设置不会删除已经下载的模型文件，但会重置眨眼动作、摄像头编号、声音和界面等设置。恢复后应重新检查摄像头，并完成一次测试呼叫。

docs.title: 向工作人员或开发者反馈
docs.text:
提交问题前，请先查看遇到问题。

如果仍然无法解决，可以通过GitHub Issues反馈，并尽量提供：

  • 软件版本和 Windows 版本。
  • 问题发生前执行的操作。
  • 主界面显示的完整提示文字。
  • 预期结果和实际结果。
  • 不包含敏感信息的截图。
  • 工作人员明确要求时提供的日志。

除非工作人员确认确有必要并说明安全的传输方式，否则不要公开上传摄像头录制。

docs.title: 提醒声音设置
docs.text:
提醒声音设置决定呼叫触发后是否响铃、使用哪种铃声、音量多大、播放多久，以及完成眨眼步骤时是否播放短提示音。

进入：

设置 → 眨眼呼叫

修改后请点击“保存”，并完成一次测试呼叫。

docs.title: 开启呼叫声音
docs.text:
将“播放呼叫音频”设为“开启”。

开启后，完成眨眼序列时软件会播放铃声，并显示呼叫提醒界面。

关闭后，完成序列时不会播放铃声，也不会显示呼叫提醒界面。软件用于日常呼叫时，建议始终保持开启。

docs.title: 选择并试听铃声
docs.text:
1. 在“呼叫音频文件”中选择铃声。
  2. 点击“试听”。
  3. 确认当前电脑或蓝牙音箱能够听到。
  4. 不合适时更换其他铃声，再次试听。

试听正常只表示声音设备和铃声可以播放。保存设置后，还需要完成一次完整的测试呼叫。

docs.title: 调整音量
docs.text:
两种声音可以分别设置音量：

  • “音频音量”：控制呼叫触发后的铃声和异常状态报警。
  • “中间提示音音量”：控制每个眨眼动作完成时的短提示音，可点击旁边的“试听”单独确认。

这里调整的是软件音量，不会改变 Windows 系统音量。实际听到的音量还会受到电脑扬声器、蓝牙音箱和 Windows 音量设置影响。

Tip

在患者实际使用的位置试听。需要跨房间提醒时，应由照护者在平时所在的位置确认能够听清。

docs.title: 设置播放时长
docs.text:
“音频播放时长”决定铃声触发后播放多久，可以选择固定时长或“无限时长”。

  • 使用固定时长时，铃声会在达到时长后停止。
  • 使用“无限时长”时，铃声会一直播放，直到患者或照护者点击红色呼叫提醒按钮。

选择时应考虑照护者通常需要多久才能听到并回应。

docs.title: 摄像头或人脸状态异常时报警
docs.text:
在“异常状态自动报警”中开启后，可以分别设置摄像头没有新画面、以及持续未检测到人脸多久后触发报警。两项默认都是 5 分钟。

报警使用当前选择的铃声和软件音量，并持续循环播放。摄像头恢复画面或重新检测到人脸后，相关报警会自动停止。点击显示“点击此按钮消音”的红色报警按钮可以手动消音；当前异常解除前不会再次响铃。此功能独立于“播放呼叫音频”开关和普通呼叫铃声时长。

docs.title: 设置眨眼步骤提示音
docs.text:
在“眨眼序列”中，每个动作步骤都有“声音提醒”选项。

开启后，患者完成当前睁眼或闭眼步骤时，软件会播放一次短提示音，表示可以继续下一个动作。这个声音与最终的呼叫铃声不同。

如果患者不方便持续观察顶部进度条，可以为关键步骤开启提示音。如果提示音容易造成干扰，也可以逐项关闭。

docs.title: 保存后的检查
docs.text:
保存设置后，请确认：

  1. 点击“试听”可以听到铃声。
  2. 软件音量和 Windows 系统音量都合适。
  3. 蓝牙音箱仍然连接在正确的播放设备上。
  4. 完成一次眨眼序列后，呼叫提醒界面出现并播放铃声。
  5. 点击红色呼叫提醒按钮可以提前停止铃声。

听不到声音时，请查看听不到提醒声音。

docs.title: 眨眼动作设置
docs.text:
眨眼动作设置决定患者需要按照怎样的顺序睁眼、闭眼，才能触发呼叫提醒。

完成首次测试前，建议先使用默认设置。需要调整时，每次只修改一项，并在保存后重新测试。

docs.title: 打开设置
docs.text:
进入：

设置 → 眨眼呼叫

确认“开启眨眼呼叫”为“开启”。建议同时保持“显示首页上方进度条”为“显示”，方便患者和照护者观察动作进度。

docs.title: 什么是眨眼序列
docs.text:
眨眼序列是一组连续的睁眼、闭眼动作。软件会按照设置顺序识别，全部完成后才触发呼叫。

当前默认序列为：

睁眼 1.5 秒 → 闭眼 1 秒 → 睁眼 1 秒 → 闭眼 1.5 秒

这套动作比自然眨眼持续时间更长，可以降低误触发的可能。

docs.title: 修改动作和持续时间
docs.text:
在“眨眼序列”中，每一行代表一个动作步骤：

  • 动作可以选择“睁眼”或“闭眼”。
  • 持续时间可以设置为 0.5 秒到 5 秒。
  • “声音提醒”决定完成该步骤时是否播放短提示音。

修改完成后点击“保存”，回到主界面完成一次测试呼叫。

docs.title: 添加或删除步骤
docs.text:
• 点击“新增步骤”可以在序列末尾增加一个动作。
  • 点击某一步右侧的“删除”可以移除该步骤。
  • 序列至少需要保留一个步骤。

步骤越多，通常越不容易与自然眨眼混淆，但患者完成动作所需的时间和体力也会增加。

docs.title: 根据实际情况调整
docs.text: 遇到的情况 可以尝试 患者闭眼比较费力 适当缩短闭眼持续时间，但不要短到容易与自然眨眼混淆 经常没有主动呼叫却响铃 延长闭眼时间，或增加一到两个动作步骤 进度经常在中途清零 适当缩短难以保持的步骤，并确认 3 秒内开始下一步 整套动作太累 缩短持续时间或减少步骤 患者不知道何时进入下一步 为相应步骤开启“声音提醒”

docs.title: 推荐的调整方法
docs.text:
1. 先记录或记住当前设置。
  2. 每次只调整一个步骤或一个持续时间。
  3. 点击“保存”并回到主界面。
  4. 让患者在舒适状态下连续测试几次。
  5. 同时观察是否容易完成、是否存在误触发。
  6. 找到合适设置后，再用于日常呼叫。

Warning

不要为了降低误触发而把动作设置得过长。患者能稳定、舒适地完成，比增加步骤更重要。

docs.title: 调整后无法正常使用
docs.text:
• 进度条不动或反复清零：查看眨眼进度不动或反复重新开始。
  • 经常误触发：查看经常在无意中触发呼叫。
  • 设置已经无法确认：使用“设置 → 其他 → 恢复默认设置”，然后重新测试。

docs.title: 摄像头设置
docs.text:
摄像头设置用于选择软件读取的摄像头，并帮助软件持续、清楚地看到患者的面部和双眼。

普通使用建议保持“本地摄像头”。只有连接多个摄像头或由工作人员配置远程摄像头时，才需要修改其他选项。

docs.title: 使用本地摄像头
docs.text:
本地摄像头是连接在当前电脑上的摄像头，例如笔记本内置摄像头或 USB 摄像头。

进入：

设置 → 摄像头 → 选择摄像头来源 → 本地摄像头

修改后点击“保存”，回到主界面检查画面。

docs.title: 选择摄像头编号
docs.text:
软件默认从编号 0 开始读取摄像头。如果主界面没有画面：

  1. 将摄像头编号设为 0，保存并检查主界面。
  2. 没有画面时，依次尝试 1、2、3。
  3. 每次修改后都要点击“保存”，再回到主界面查看。

Windows 可能同时列出内置摄像头、USB 摄像头、红外摄像头和虚拟摄像头。请以主界面能否显示正常彩色画面为准。

正常画面的标志

主界面能够连续显示患者画面，没有出现“摄像头不可用”或“正在尝试恢复”等文字提示。

docs.title: 调整画面
docs.text:
请调整摄像头或患者位置，直到：

  • 患者面向摄像头。
  • 面部和双眼完整出现在画面中。
  • 双眼不要离画面边缘太近。
  • 双眼没有被头发、被子、手或眼镜边框遮挡。
  • 面部光线稳定，不过暗，也没有强烈背光。
  • 患者可以自然、舒适地保持当前位置。

如果画面正常但软件检测不到患者，请查看检测不到患者面部或双眼。

docs.title: 摄像头断开后的恢复
docs.text:
本地摄像头短暂断开时，软件会在后台自动尝试重新连接。

如果只有一个外接摄像头：

  1. 保持软件运行。
  2. 检查连接线并重新插入摄像头。
  3. 等待主界面从“正在尝试恢复”重新变成摄像头画面。

这种情况下不需要启用备用摄像头。

docs.title: 使用备用摄像头
docs.text:
笔记本同时拥有内置和外接摄像头时，可以将其中一个设置为备用摄像头。

  1. 先分别测试两个摄像头编号，确认它们都能显示正常画面。
  2. 进入“设置 → 摄像头”，选择“本地摄像头”。
  3. 将常用摄像头设为主摄像头编号。
  4. 开启“启用备用摄像头”。
  5. 填写一个与主摄像头不同的备用摄像头编号。
  6. 点击“保存”，再完成一次测试呼叫。

如果主摄像头暂时无法使用，软件会等待几秒后切换到备用摄像头。切换后，只要备用摄像头能够正常使用，软件会继续使用它，不会因为主摄像头恢复就马上来回切换。如果备用摄像头也无法使用，软件会再次尝试主摄像头。

不要把虚拟摄像头设置为备用摄像头。

docs.title: 使用远程摄像头（进阶）
docs.text:
远程摄像头适合摄像头连接在另一台电脑上的情况，需要两台电脑处于可以互相访问的网络中。建议由熟悉网络配置的工作人员完成。

在连接摄像头的电脑上：

  1. 打开“设置 → 摄像头”。
  2. 在“启动本地摄像头服务”处选择摄像头编号和服务端口。
  3. 点击“启动本地摄像头服务”。
  4. 记录主界面显示的地址和端口。

在运行眨眼识别的电脑上：

  1. 打开“设置 → 摄像头”。
  2. 选择“远程摄像头”。
  3. 填写摄像头服务电脑显示的地址和端口。
  4. 点击“保存”，回到主界面检查画面。

如果主界面显示“远程摄像头不可用”，请检查两台电脑的网络、地址和端口是否一致，并确认提供摄像头画面的电脑仍在运行服务。

docs.title: 摄像头仍然不可用
docs.text: 请查看摄像头没有画面。提交问题时请说明使用的是本地、备用还是远程摄像头，以及尝试过的摄像头编号。

docs.title: 日常使用
docs.text: 完成首次配置后，日常使用只需要打开软件、检查摄像头和声音，然后按当前设置的眨眼序列触发呼叫。

docs.title: 使用前快速检查
docs.text:
每次开始使用时，请由家属或照护者确认：

  • BlinkCall.exe 已经打开。
  • 主界面正在连续显示摄像头画面。
  • 患者的面部和双眼完整、清楚，没有被遮挡。
  • 顶部眨眼进度条可见。
  • 电脑扬声器或蓝牙音箱已经连接，音量合适。

Tip

更换摄像头、移动电脑、改变患者位置或修改眨眼动作后，应重新完成一次测试呼叫。

docs.title: 触发呼叫
docs.text:
按照当前设置的顺序完成睁眼、闭眼动作。

软件当前的默认序列为：

睁眼 1.5 秒 → 闭眼 1 秒 → 睁眼 1 秒 → 闭眼 1.5 秒

如果已经自定义过动作，请以软件设置中显示的“眨眼序列”为准。

docs.title: 看懂顶部进度条
docs.text:
顶部进度条显示当前需要完成的动作以及完成进度：

  • 浅绿色表示睁眼阶段。
  • 浅黄色表示闭眼阶段。
  • 深绿色表示当前已经完成的进度。

每个阶段都要保持当前状态，直到该阶段完成。完成一个阶段后，请在 3 秒内开始下一个阶段，否则整个序列会重新开始。

docs.title: 呼叫触发后
docs.text:
完成整个序列后，软件会播放提醒声音并显示呼叫提醒界面。

如果设置了固定播放时长，铃声会在达到时长后停止。如果设置为“无限时长”，铃声会持续播放，直到有人停止。

如需提前停止，患者或照护者可以点击红色呼叫提醒按钮。

docs.title: 使用过程中需要注意
docs.text:
• 不要让头发、被子、手或眼镜边框遮挡双眼。
  • 环境光线或患者位置发生明显变化时，重新检查识别效果。
  • 摄像头短暂断开时，软件会自动尝试恢复；重新插入后请等待画面恢复。
  • 铃声必须足以让照护者听到，尤其是在房间距离较远或环境嘈杂时。
  • 如果患者完成动作感到疲劳，请在照护者协助下调整序列，不要勉强完成过长的动作。

docs.title: 登录后自动启动和系统托盘
docs.text:
在 设置 → 常规 中开启“任意用户登录后自动启动”并保存后，BlinkCall 会注册 Windows 守护服务。服务会在任意活动用户会话中启动 BlinkCall；程序意外退出或被强制结束时会自动重启。启用或关闭该功能需要管理员授权；如果当前程序未以管理员身份运行，Windows 会自动弹出授权提示，请按提示确认。

软件启动后会显示在系统托盘中。点击窗口右上角的关闭按钮会隐藏到托盘，右键托盘图标可以重新显示窗口或退出软件。

如需关闭自动启动，请取消“任意用户登录后自动启动”并保存设置。

docs.title: 没有正常触发
docs.text:
请先观察主界面显示的内容：

  • 没有画面：查看摄像头没有画面。
  • 显示未检测到人脸或关键点无效：查看检测不到患者面部或双眼。
  • 进度条不动或反复清零：查看眨眼进度不动或反复重新开始。
  • 呼叫出现但没有声音：查看听不到提醒声音。

docs.title: 首次使用
docs.text: 本页适合第一次为患者配置软件的家属或照护者阅读。完成后，你应该能够看到稳定的摄像头画面，并成功触发一次有声音的测试呼叫。

docs.title: 操作演示
docs.text:
可以先观看操作演示，再按照下面的步骤完成配置和测试。视频使用中文界面，时长约 2 分 22 秒。

您的浏览器不支持内嵌视频。

无法播放时，可以打开或下载视频。

docs.title: 1. 准备设备
docs.text:
开始前请准备：

  • 一台 Windows 电脑。
  • 电脑内置摄像头或 USB 摄像头。
  • 电脑扬声器或蓝牙音箱。
  • 可用的网络连接，用于首次下载模型文件。

建议让患者和照护者一起完成最后的测试。

docs.title: 2. 下载并解压软件
docs.text:
从下面任意一个地址下载最新的软件压缩包：

  • GitHub 最新版本
  • 百度网盘
  • 夸克网盘

下载完成后：

  1. 找到软件压缩包。
  2. 将压缩包完整解压到一个固定位置。
  3. 打开解压后的文件夹。

不要直接在压缩包内运行软件。

docs.title: 3. 打开软件
docs.text:
在解压后的文件夹中双击 BlinkCall.exe。

软件打开后，会进入主界面。模型文件和摄像头准备完成后，主界面会显示摄像头画面和顶部的眨眼进度条。

软件无法打开？

确认已经完整解压软件，并再次从解压后的文件夹中运行。如果仍然无法打开，请查看软件无法打开。

docs.title: 4. 下载模型文件
docs.text:
第一次使用时必须先下载模型文件。

  1. 点击主界面左上角的“设置”。
  2. 在左侧选择“眨眼呼叫”。
  3. 找到“下载/更新模型文件”。
  4. 点击“下载/更新”，等待进度完成。

完成标志

下载成功后，下载进度窗口会关闭，设置会自动保存。返回主界面后，不再显示“未检测到模型文件”的提示。

下载没有成功

如果页面提示网络连接超时、网络连接失败或下载模型文件失败，请检查网络后重新尝试。详细步骤请查看模型文件下载失败。

docs.title: 5. 允许摄像头权限
docs.text:
如果 Windows 弹出摄像头权限提示，请选择允许。

如果没有弹窗，可以继续下一步。之后仍然看不到画面时，再到 Windows 的摄像头隐私设置中检查权限。

docs.title: 6. 选择摄像头
docs.text:
软件默认使用本地摄像头，摄像头编号为 0。

如果主界面没有画面：

  1. 打开“设置 → 摄像头”。
  2. 保持选择“本地摄像头”。
  3. 将摄像头编号设为 0，点击“保存”并检查主界面。
  4. 如果仍无画面，依次尝试 1、2、3，每次修改后都要保存。

完成标志

主界面能够连续显示摄像头画面，而不是“摄像头不可用”或“正在尝试恢复”等文字提示。

连接多个摄像头或需要备用摄像头时，请查看摄像头设置。

docs.title: 7. 调整患者和摄像头的位置
docs.text:
请调整摄像头或患者位置，直到：

  • 患者面向摄像头，面部和双眼完整出现在画面中。
  • 双眼没有被头发、被子、手或眼镜边框遮挡。
  • 画面光线稳定，面部不过暗。
  • 患者能够自然、舒适地保持当前位置。

如果主界面显示“未检测到人脸”“人脸关键点定位失败”或“关键点无效”，请查看检测不到患者面部或双眼。

docs.title: 8. 完成一次测试呼叫
docs.text:
当前默认眨眼序列为：

睁眼 1.5 秒 → 闭眼 1 秒 → 睁眼 1 秒 → 闭眼 1.5 秒

测试时：

  1. 观察主界面顶部的进度条。
  2. 按顺序保持睁眼或闭眼，直到当前阶段完成。
  3. 完成一个阶段后，在 3 秒内开始下一个阶段。
  4. 完成整个序列后，等待呼叫提醒界面出现并确认铃声响起。
  5. 点击红色呼叫提醒按钮，提前停止铃声。

测试完成

同时满足以下条件，表示首次配置成功：

  • 摄像头画面连续、清楚。
  • 顶部进度条会跟随睁眼、闭眼动作前进。
  • 完成序列后出现呼叫提醒界面。
  • 电脑或蓝牙音箱能够听到铃声。
  • 点击红色呼叫提醒按钮可以停止铃声。

如果进度不动、总是重新开始或没有声音，请进入遇到问题。

docs.title: 下一步
docs.text:
• 日常使用前的检查方法：日常使用
  • 根据患者情况调整动作：眨眼动作设置
  • 调整铃声和音量：提醒声音设置

docs.title: 快速开始
docs.text: 这一部分帮助家属或照护者完成第一次配置，并掌握日常呼叫方法。

docs.title: 第一次使用流程
docs.text:
1. 下载并解压软件：将软件放在一个固定位置。
  2. 打开软件：双击 BlinkCall.exe。
  3. 下载模型文件：进入“设置 → 眨眼呼叫 → 下载/更新模型文件”。
  4. 确认摄像头画面：允许摄像头权限，让患者的双眼完整出现在画面中。
  5. 完成测试呼叫：按照顶部进度条完成默认眨眼序列，确认提醒声音正常。

完整步骤、截图和成功标志请查看首次使用。

docs.title: 日常使用流程
docs.text:
1. 打开软件。
  2. 确认摄像头画面连续、清楚。
  3. 确认患者双眼没有被遮挡。
  4. 按当前设置完成眨眼序列。
  5. 如需提前结束铃声，由照护者点击红色呼叫提醒按钮。

详细说明请查看日常使用。

docs.title: 如果中途遇到问题
docs.text:
• 软件无法打开或模型文件下载失败。
  • 摄像头没有画面，或者画面中检测不到人脸。
  • 眨眼进度不动、无法触发或经常误触发。
  • 呼叫已经触发，但听不到提醒声音。

遇到以上情况，请进入遇到问题。

docs.title: 配置完成的标准
docs.text:
完成首次配置后，应同时满足以下条件：

  • 主界面能够连续显示患者画面。
  • 顶部进度条能够跟随睁眼、闭眼动作变化。
  • 患者可以在不过度疲劳的情况下完成眨眼序列。
  • 完成序列后，照护者能够听到提醒声音。
  • 照护者能够停止提醒，并知道在哪里调整动作、摄像头和声音。

docs.title: 设置
docs.text:
完成首次测试后，可以根据患者的实际情况调整软件。日常使用一般不需要频繁修改设置。

打开主界面左上角的“设置”，修改完成后点击“保存”。

免责声明

本工具仅用于辅助看护，不能替代人工看护。请勿因使用本工具而减少或免除必要的人工看护。

docs.title: 我想调整什么
docs.text: 需要调整的内容 前往页面 建议 呼叫需要完成哪些睁眼、闭眼动作 眨眼动作设置 先使用默认设置测试，再逐项微调 使用哪个摄像头，或者启用备用摄像头 摄像头设置 普通使用保持“本地摄像头” 铃声、音量、播放时长和步骤提示音 提醒声音设置 保存前先试听，并检查系统音量 摄像头或人脸长时间未检测到时报警 提醒声音设置 可分别设置两种异常的报警等待时长 语言、亮暗模式、录制、日志和恢复默认值 其他设置与技术支持 录制和日志通常只在排查问题时开启

docs.title: 修改设置时的建议
docs.text:
• 每次只修改一类设置，保存后立即完成一次测试呼叫。
  • 调整眨眼动作时，以患者能稳定完成且不过度疲劳为准。
  • 调整摄像头后，回到主界面确认画面连续、双眼清楚可见。
  • 调整声音后，同时检查软件音量和电脑或蓝牙音箱的音量。
  • 如果设置被改乱，可以在“设置 → 其他 → 恢复默认设置”中恢复，然后重新测试。

docs.title: 设置没有生效
docs.text: 请确认已经点击设置窗口底部的“保存”。如果问题仍然存在，请查看遇到问题。

docs.title: 遇到问题
docs.text: 遇到问题时，先观察主界面的画面和文字提示，再选择对应的排查方法。

docs.title: 先完成这几个检查
docs.text:
1. 确认软件已经完整解压，不是在压缩包内运行。
  2. 确认模型文件已经下载完成。
  3. 确认摄像头画面连续、清楚，患者面部和双眼完整可见。
  4. 确认“设置 → 眨眼呼叫 → 开启眨眼呼叫”处于开启状态。
  5. 确认电脑或蓝牙音箱没有静音。

如果问题仍然存在，请继续查看下面对应的情况。

docs.title: 软件无法打开
docs.text:
请依次检查：

  1. 确认已经将下载的软件压缩包完整解压。
  2. 进入解压后的文件夹，双击 BlinkCall.exe。
  3. 不要移动或单独复制 BlinkCall.exe，它需要和文件夹中的其他文件放在一起。
  4. 重新下载软件压缩包并解压到一个新的文件夹，再次尝试。

仍然无法打开时，请记录 Windows 版本、软件版本和屏幕上的提示，然后通过GitHub Issues反馈。

docs.title: 模型文件下载失败
docs.text:
如果页面显示“网络连接超时”“网络连接失败”“请求模型信息失败”或“下载模型文件失败”：

  1. 确认电脑能够正常访问网络。
  2. 关闭下载提示后，重新进入“设置 → 眨眼呼叫”。
  3. 再次点击“下载/更新”。
  4. 等待整个进度完成，不要在下载过程中关闭软件。

下载成功后，进度窗口会关闭，设置会自动保存。主界面不再显示“未检测到模型文件”的提示。

如果多次尝试仍然失败，请记录页面显示的完整错误文字，并通过GitHub Issues反馈。

docs.title: 摄像头没有画面
docs.text:
如果主界面显示“摄像头不可用”：

  1. 确认摄像头已经正确连接。
  2. 检查 Windows 是否允许桌面应用访问摄像头。
  3. 关闭可能正在占用摄像头的会议、直播或拍照软件。
  4. 打开“设置 → 摄像头”，选择“本地摄像头”。
  5. 从编号 0 开始尝试；没有画面时依次尝试 1、2、3。
  6. 每次修改编号后点击“保存”，回到主界面检查。

如果主界面显示“摄像头连接中断，正在尝试恢复”，请检查连接线并重新插入摄像头，然后等待软件自动恢复。

使用笔记本内置摄像头和外接摄像头时，可以设置备用摄像头。详细说明请查看摄像头设置。

docs.title: 检测不到患者面部或双眼
docs.text:
主界面可能显示：

  • “未检测到人脸”
  • “人脸关键点定位失败”
  • “关键点无效，请检查患者姿态或眼部遮挡”

请调整摄像头或患者位置：

  1. 让患者面向摄像头。
  2. 确保完整面部和双眼都在画面中，不要靠近画面边缘。
  3. 移开遮挡双眼的头发、被子、手或眼镜边框。
  4. 改善面部光线，避免面部过暗或强烈背光。
  5. 保持患者和摄像头位置稳定，等待画面恢复识别。

docs.title: 眨眼进度不动或反复重新开始
docs.text:
请检查：

  1. “设置 → 眨眼呼叫 → 开启眨眼呼叫”是否为“开启”。
  2. “显示首页上方进度条”是否为“显示”。
  3. 患者面部和双眼是否能够被持续识别。
  4. 每个睁眼或闭眼动作是否保持到当前阶段完成。
  5. 完成一个阶段后，是否在 3 秒内开始了下一个阶段。
  6. 当前实际动作是否与“设置 → 眨眼呼叫 → 眨眼序列”一致。

建议先恢复默认设置并测试默认序列。默认序列为：

睁眼 1.5 秒 → 闭眼 1 秒 → 睁眼 1 秒 → 闭眼 1.5 秒

如果患者难以完成当前动作，请查看眨眼动作设置。

docs.title: 完成序列但没有触发呼叫
docs.text:
1. 确认整个序列都已完成，进度没有在中途清零。
  2. 确认“开启眨眼呼叫”处于开启状态。
  3. 确认模型文件没有缺失或损坏；可以在“下载/更新模型文件”处重新检查。
  4. 点击“保存”后返回主界面，再完成一次测试。

如果主界面显示“推理异常”或“眨眼功能异常”，请先关闭并重新打开软件。问题持续出现时，请记录提示文字并提交问题。

docs.title: 经常在无意中触发呼叫
docs.text:
• 不要只使用很短的闭眼动作，以免与自然眨眼混淆。
  • 适当延长闭眼持续时间。
  • 增加一到两个动作步骤，让完整序列更容易与自然眨眼区分。
  • 每次只修改一项，然后连续测试几次。
  • 调整时兼顾患者体力，不要把序列设置得过长。

具体设置方法请查看眨眼动作设置。

docs.title: 听不到提醒声音
docs.text:
1. 打开“设置 → 眨眼呼叫”。
  2. 确认“播放呼叫音频”为“开启”。
  3. 选择一个呼叫音频文件并点击“试听”。
  4. 调高软件中的“音频音量”。
  5. 检查 Windows 系统音量以及扬声器或蓝牙音箱音量。
  6. 使用蓝牙音箱时，确认电脑仍然连接到正确的播放设备。
  7. 保存设置并重新完成一次测试呼叫。

如果“试听”有声音，但触发呼叫后没有声音，请确认呼叫序列是否真的完成，以及呼叫提醒界面是否出现。

docs.title: 设置被改乱
docs.text:
进入“设置 → 其他 → 恢复默认设置”，确认恢复后重新完成一次测试呼叫。

恢复默认设置会重置眨眼动作、摄像头、声音和界面等配置，不会删除已经下载的模型文件。

docs.title: 提交问题时请提供
docs.text:
通过GitHub Issues反馈时，建议提供：

  • 眨眼呼叫版本号。
  • Windows 版本。
  • 问题发生前执行了哪些操作。
  • 预期看到什么，以及实际看到了什么。
  • 主界面显示的完整提示文字。
  • 能够帮助说明问题的截图。

如果工作人员需要日志或摄像头录制，会进一步说明如何获取。摄像头录制可能包含患者面部和周围环境，请先征得同意，不要在公开问题中直接上传敏感画面。

docs.title: Blink Call User Manual
docs.text:
Blink Call is an assistive call system designed for ALS patients. After the patient completes a preset sequence of eye-open and eye-closed actions, the computer or a Bluetooth speaker plays an alert to notify family members or caregivers.

Download the Latest Version First Use Troubleshooting

Disclaimer

This tool is intended only to support caregiving and cannot replace human supervision. Do not reduce or omit necessary human supervision because you use this tool.

Applicable Version

This manual applies to Blink Call v1.8.0. Currently, only the Windows version is available for direct download and use.

docs.title: I Am Using the Software for the First Time
docs.text: Follow First Use to download and extract the software, download model files, set up the camera, and complete a test call.

docs.title: Setup Is Already Complete
docs.text: Read Daily Use for the checks to make before each use and instructions for triggering and stopping calls.

docs.title: The Software Is Not Working Properly
docs.text: Open Troubleshooting to check the software, model files, camera, blink recognition, and audio.

docs.title: Who This Is For
docs.text:
• People who have difficulty speaking and cannot easily call out for help.
  • People who have difficulty using their hands and cannot reliably press buttons or use a physical call device.
  • People who can complete simple eye-open and eye-closed actions.
  • Patients whose family members or caregivers can assist with initial setup and testing.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
• A Windows computer.
  • A camera that can clearly capture both of the patient's eyes.
  • Computer speakers or a Bluetooth speaker.
  • An internet connection for the first model download.

docs.title: Download the Software
docs.text:
Choose any one of these download options:

  • GitHub Latest Release
  • Baidu Netdisk
  • Quark Netdisk

Fully extract the downloaded package to a fixed location, then double-click BlinkCall.exe in the extracted folder. Do not run the software from inside the compressed package.

docs.title: Before Daily Use Begins
docs.text:
Have the patient and caregiver complete at least one test call together and confirm that:

  • The camera view is continuous and clear, with both eyes fully visible.
  • The patient can complete the configured blink sequence.
  • The computer or Bluetooth speaker alert can be heard clearly.
  • The caregiver knows how to stop the alert.

Repeat the test after changes to the software or environment, such as replacing the camera, moving the computer, or adjusting the blink pattern.

docs.title: Free to Use
docs.text: This software is completely free and non-profit.

docs.title: Advanced Settings and Technical Support
docs.text: This page covers language, appearance, and the recording, logging, and restore-default options used for troubleshooting. Recording and debug mode are usually unnecessary for daily calls.

docs.title: Switch Language
docs.text:
Open:

Settings → General → Language

Choose Chinese or English. Click Save to switch the interface to the selected language.

docs.title: Change Theme
docs.text:
Open:

Settings → General → Theme

Choose Light or Dark. This changes the appearance only and does not affect camera recognition or calling.

docs.title: Record Current Camera Data
docs.text:
This feature saves a recording of the current camera view to help developers or staff investigate recognition problems. It is not needed for ordinary daily use.

Open:

Settings → Others → Record current camera data

To record:

  1. Set the maximum recording duration.
  2. Select a local folder.
  3. Click Start recording.
  4. The software returns to the main screen and starts recording.
  5. To finish early, click the stop-recording button on the main screen.

Protect Patient Privacy

A camera recording may contain the patient's face and surroundings. Obtain consent from the patient or guardian before recording or sharing. Do not upload sensitive footage directly to a public GitHub issue.

docs.title: Enable Debug Mode and Logs
docs.text:
Debug mode displays information about software operation. Enable it when staff need to examine recognition status or investigate a problem.

Open:

Settings → Others → Debug mode

To save the general debug log to a file:

  1. Turn on Debug mode.
  2. Set Save to local to Yes.
  3. Choose the local log folder.
  4. Click Save and repeat the actions until the problem occurs again.

When debug mode is enabled, the selected log folder also receives a separate audio_status.log. It records audio-output changes, the ringtone file and volume, load/play states, play requests, and stop events to help investigate a call that was triggered without sound. The file is rotated and keeps recent records.

After troubleshooting, you can turn off debug mode so technical information no longer remains on the main screen.

docs.title: Restore Defaults
docs.text:
If blink, camera, audio, or interface settings have become confusing, open:

Settings → Others → Restore defaults

After confirmation, the software restores the default configuration and closes the settings window.

Restoring defaults does not delete downloaded model files. It resets the blink pattern, camera ID, audio, interface, and other settings. Check the camera and complete a test call afterwards.

docs.title: Contact Staff or Developers
docs.text:
Read Troubleshooting before submitting a report.

If the problem remains, report it through GitHub Issues and include:

  • The software version and Windows version.
  • The actions taken before the problem occurred.
  • The complete message shown on the main screen.
  • What you expected and what actually happened.
  • Screenshots without sensitive information.
  • Logs, if staff specifically request them.

Do not publicly upload camera recordings unless staff confirm they are needed and explain a safe way to transfer them.

docs.title: Audio Alert
docs.text:
Audio settings determine whether calls ring, which ringtone is used, its volume and playback duration, and whether short cues play after blink steps.

Open:

Settings → Blink Call

After making changes, click Save and complete a test call.

docs.title: Enable Call Audio
docs.text:
Set Play call audio to On.

When enabled, completing the blink sequence plays the ringtone and displays the call alert.

When disabled, completing the sequence does not play the call ringtone or display the call alert. Keep it enabled for daily calls.

docs.title: Select and Preview a Ringtone
docs.text:
1. Select a ringtone under Call audio file.
  2. Click Preview.
  3. Confirm that it can be heard through the computer or Bluetooth speaker.
  4. If needed, choose another ringtone and preview it again.

A successful preview confirms only that the sound device and ringtone can play. After saving, complete a full test call as well.

docs.title: Adjust the Volume
docs.text:
The two sounds have separate volume controls:

  • Audio volume controls the call ringtone and automatic abnormality alerts.
  • Stage prompt volume controls the short cue after each blink step. Click Preview next to it to check the cue separately.

These controls do not change the Windows system volume. The sound you hear also depends on the computer speakers, Bluetooth speaker, and Windows volume settings.

Tip

Preview the sounds at the patient's actual location. If the alert needs to be heard across rooms, have the caregiver check it from their usual location.

docs.title: Set the Playback Duration
docs.text:
Audio play duration determines how long a call ringtone plays. Choose a fixed duration or Unlimited.

  • With a fixed duration, the ringtone stops when the configured time is reached.
  • With Unlimited, it continues until the patient or caregiver clicks the red call alert button.

Consider how long the caregiver usually needs to hear and respond to an alert.

docs.title: Alert When the Camera or Face Is Missing
docs.text:
Turn on Automatic abnormality alert to set separate delays for a camera without new frames and a face that remains undetected. Both delays default to 5 minutes.

The alert uses the selected ringtone and Audio volume, and loops continuously. The relevant alert stops automatically when the camera view or face detection recovers. To silence it manually, click the red alarm button labeled Tap to silence; it will not ring again until the current abnormal condition clears. This feature works independently of Play call audio and the normal call playback duration.

docs.title: Set Blink Step Prompt Sounds
docs.text:
Each action under Blink sequence has a Sound prompt option.

When enabled, the software plays a short cue after the patient completes that eye-open or eye-closed step, indicating that they can continue to the next action. This cue is different from the final call ringtone.

Enable cues for key steps if watching the progress bar continuously is difficult. If the cues are distracting, disable them individually.

docs.title: Check After Saving
docs.text:
After saving the settings, confirm that:

  1. Preview plays the ringtone.
  2. The software volume and Windows volume are appropriate.
  3. The Bluetooth speaker remains connected as the correct playback device.
  4. Completing a blink sequence displays the call alert and plays the ringtone.
  5. Clicking the red call alert button stops the ringtone early.

If you cannot hear the alert, see No Alert Sound.

docs.title: Blink Pattern
docs.text:
Blink pattern settings determine the order of eye-open and eye-closed actions needed to trigger a call alert.

Use the default settings until the first test succeeds. When adjusting them, change one setting at a time and test again after saving.

docs.title: Open the Settings
docs.text:
Open:

Settings → Blink Call

Make sure Enable blink call is set to On. Keep Show top progress bar on home page set to Show so the patient and caregiver can follow the actions.

docs.title: What Is a Blink Sequence?
docs.text:
A blink sequence is a series of eye-open and eye-closed actions. The software recognizes them in the configured order and triggers a call only after the complete sequence finishes.

The current default sequence is:

Eyes open for 1.5 seconds → eyes closed for 1 second → eyes open for 1 second → eyes closed for 1.5 seconds.

These actions last longer than a natural blink, which helps reduce accidental calls.

docs.title: Change Actions and Durations
docs.text:
Each row under Blink sequence is one action step:

  • Choose Open eyes or Close eyes.
  • Set the duration from 0.5 to 5 seconds.
  • Sound prompt determines whether a short cue plays when the step finishes.

Click Save, return to the main screen, and complete a test call.

docs.title: Add or Remove Steps
docs.text:
• Click Add step to append an action to the sequence.
  • Click Remove on the right of a step to delete it.
  • At least one step must remain.

More steps usually make the sequence harder to confuse with natural blinking, but also take more time and effort to complete.

docs.title: Adjust for the Patient
docs.text: Situation What to try Closing the eyes is difficult Shorten the eye-closed duration without making it easy to confuse with natural blinking The alert sounds without an intentional call Increase the eye-closed duration or add one or two action steps Progress often resets midway Shorten difficult steps and make sure the next step starts within 3 seconds The complete sequence is too tiring Shorten durations or reduce the number of steps The patient does not know when to move on Enable Sound prompt for the relevant steps

docs.title: A Suggested Adjustment Process
docs.text:
1. Record or remember the current settings.
  2. Adjust only one step or duration at a time.
  3. Click Save and return to the main screen.
  4. Have the patient test several times while comfortable.
  5. Check both ease of completion and accidental triggering.
  6. Use the settings for daily calls after finding a suitable sequence.

Warning

Do not make actions excessively long just to reduce accidental calls. The patient's ability to complete them reliably and comfortably matters more than adding steps.

docs.title: Problems After Adjusting
docs.text:
• Progress does not move or keeps resetting: see Blink Progress Does Not Move or Keeps Resetting.
  • Accidental calls: see Calls Are Triggered Accidentally.
  • The settings are no longer clear: use Settings → Others → Restore defaults, then test again.

docs.title: Camera
docs.text:
Camera settings select the camera used by the software and help keep the patient's face and both eyes clearly visible.

For ordinary use, keep Local camera selected. Other options are needed when multiple cameras are connected or staff are setting up a remote camera.

docs.title: Use a Local Camera
docs.text:
A local camera is connected to the current computer, such as a laptop's built-in camera or a USB camera.

Open:

Settings → Camera → Choose camera source → Local camera

After making changes, click Save and check the main screen.

docs.title: Select the Camera ID
docs.text:
The software starts with camera ID 0 by default. If no image appears:

  1. Set the camera ID to 0, save, and check the main screen.
  2. If no image appears, try 1, 2, and 3 in order.
  3. Click Save after each change, then check the main screen again.

Windows may list built-in, USB, infrared, and virtual cameras. Choose an ID that produces a normal color image on the main screen.

Signs of a Working Camera

The main screen continuously shows the patient, without camera-unavailable or reconnecting messages.

docs.title: Adjust the View
docs.text:
Adjust the camera or the patient's position until:

  • The patient faces the camera.
  • The full face and both eyes are in view.
  • The eyes are not too close to the edges of the image.
  • Hair, bedding, hands, or eyeglass frames do not cover the eyes.
  • Lighting on the face is stable, without excessive darkness or strong backlighting.
  • The patient can maintain the position naturally and comfortably.

If the view looks normal but the patient is not detected, see The Patient's Face or Eyes Are Not Detected.

docs.title: Recovery After Disconnection
docs.text:
The software automatically tries to reconnect a local camera after a temporary disconnection.

If there is only one external camera:

  1. Keep the software running.
  2. Check the cable and reconnect the camera.
  3. Wait for the reconnecting message to be replaced by the camera view.

A fallback camera does not need to be enabled in this situation.

docs.title: Use a Fallback Camera
docs.text:
If a laptop has both a built-in camera and an external camera, one can serve as the fallback.

  1. Test both camera IDs separately and confirm that each produces a normal image.
  2. Open Settings → Camera and select Local camera.
  3. Enter the ID of the camera normally used as the primary camera.
  4. Turn on Enable fallback camera.
  5. Enter a fallback camera ID different from the primary ID.
  6. Click Save and complete a test call.

If the primary camera remains unavailable, the software waits a few seconds and switches to the fallback. It keeps using the fallback while that camera works, even if the primary recovers, to prevent repeated switching. If the fallback also becomes unavailable, the software tries the primary again.

Do not use a virtual camera as the fallback. Check that the chosen device provides a usable image rather than an infrared feed.

docs.title: Use a Remote Camera (Advanced)
docs.text:
A remote camera is connected to another computer. Both computers must be on a network where they can reach each other. Staff familiar with network configuration should perform this setup.

On the computer connected to the camera:

  1. Open Settings → Camera.
  2. Under Start local camera service, choose the camera ID and service port.
  3. Click Start local camera service.
  4. Note the address and port shown on the main screen.

On the computer running blink recognition:

  1. Open Settings → Camera.
  2. Select Remote camera.
  3. Enter the address and port shown by the camera-service computer.
  4. Click Save and check the main screen.

If the main screen says the remote camera is unavailable, check the network, address, and port on both computers. Make sure the computer supplying the camera view is still running the service.

docs.title: The Camera Is Still Unavailable
docs.text: See No Camera Image. When reporting the problem, state whether you use a local, fallback, or remote camera and which camera IDs you have tried.

docs.title: Daily Use
docs.text: After initial setup, open the software, check the camera and audio, then complete the configured blink sequence to trigger a call.

docs.title: Quick Checks Before Use
docs.text:
Before each use, have a family member or caregiver confirm that:

  • BlinkCall.exe is open.
  • The main screen continuously shows the camera view.
  • The patient's face and both eyes are fully visible, clear, and uncovered.
  • The top blink progress bar is visible.
  • The computer speakers or Bluetooth speaker are connected and the volume is appropriate.

Tip

Repeat a test call after replacing the camera, moving the computer, changing the patient's position, or adjusting the blink pattern.

docs.title: Trigger a Call
docs.text:
Complete the eye-open and eye-closed actions in the configured order.

The current default sequence is:

Eyes open for 1.5 seconds → eyes closed for 1 second → eyes open for 1 second → eyes closed for 1.5 seconds.

If you have customized the actions, follow Blink sequence in the settings.

docs.title: Understand the Top Progress Bar
docs.text:
The progress bar shows the required action and completion progress:

  • Light green: eyes-open stage.
  • Light yellow: eyes-closed stage.
  • Dark green: completed progress.

Hold the current action until its stage finishes. Start the next stage within 3 seconds of finishing the previous one, or the whole sequence resets.

docs.title: After a Call Is Triggered
docs.text:
After the whole sequence finishes, the software plays the ringtone and displays the call alert.

With a fixed playback duration, the ringtone stops when the configured time is reached. With Unlimited, it continues until someone stops it.

To stop early, the patient or caregiver can click the red call alert button.

docs.title: During Use
docs.text:
• Keep hair, bedding, hands, and eyeglass frames away from the eyes.
  • Check recognition again after a significant change in lighting or patient position.
  • If the camera disconnects briefly, the software automatically tries to recover. Reconnect the device and wait for the view to return.
  • The alert must be audible to the caregiver, especially across rooms or in noisy surroundings.
  • If the sequence is tiring, adjust it with a caregiver's help rather than asking the patient to complete excessively long actions.

docs.title: Start Automatically and Use the System Tray
docs.text:
In Settings → General, enable Start automatically when any user logs in and save the settings. BlinkCall registers a Windows watchdog service that starts the app in each active user session and restarts it after an unexpected exit or forced termination. Enabling or disabling this feature requires administrator authorization. If BlinkCall is not already running as an administrator, Windows automatically displays an authorization prompt; approve it to apply the change.

After startup, BlinkCall remains available in the system tray. Closing the window hides it to the tray; right-click the tray icon to show the window again or exit the application.

To disable automatic startup, clear Start automatically when any user logs in and save the settings.

docs.title: A Call Did Not Trigger Normally
docs.text:
Check what the main screen shows:

  • No image: see No Camera Image.
  • No face detected or invalid keypoints: see The Patient's Face or Eyes Are Not Detected.
  • Progress does not move or keeps resetting: see Blink Progress Does Not Move or Keeps Resetting.
  • The call alert appears without sound: see No Alert Sound.

docs.title: First Use
docs.text: This page is for family members or caregivers setting up the software for a patient for the first time. When finished, you should have a stable camera view and be able to trigger a test call with an audible alert.

docs.title: Quick Start Video
docs.text:
Watch the demonstration before following the setup and test steps below. The video uses the Chinese interface and lasts about 2 minutes 22 seconds. The screenshots also show the Chinese interface.

Your browser does not support embedded video.

If playback is unavailable, open or download the video.

docs.title: 1. Prepare the Equipment
docs.text:
Before starting, prepare:

  • A Windows computer.
  • A built-in camera or USB camera.
  • Computer speakers or a Bluetooth speaker.
  • An internet connection for the first model download.

Have the patient and caregiver complete the final test together.

docs.title: 2. Download and Extract the Software
docs.text:
Download the latest software package from any one of these links:

  • GitHub Latest Release
  • Baidu Netdisk
  • Quark Netdisk

After downloading:

  1. Find the software package.
  2. Fully extract it to a fixed location.
  3. Open the extracted folder.

Do not run the software directly inside the compressed package.

docs.title: 3. Open the Software
docs.text:
Double-click BlinkCall.exe in the extracted folder.

The software opens to the main screen. Once the model files and camera are ready, it shows the camera view and the blink progress bar at the top.

The Software Will Not Open?

Check that the software is fully extracted and run it from the extracted folder again. If it still will not open, see The Software Will Not Open.

docs.title: 4. Download the Model Files
docs.text:
Model files must be downloaded before first use.

  1. Click Settings at the top left of the main screen.
  2. Select Blink Call on the left.
  3. Find Download/Update model files.
  4. Click Download/Update and wait for the download to finish.

Signs of Success

After a successful download, the software automatically saves the settings, closes the settings window, and returns to the main screen. The message that model files are missing should no longer appear.

The Download Did Not Finish

If the software reports a network timeout, connection failure, or model download failure, check the connection and try again. See Model Files Will Not Download for details.

docs.title: 5. Allow Camera Access
docs.text:
If Windows asks for camera permission, allow access.

If no prompt appears, continue to the next step. If there is still no image afterwards, check Windows camera privacy settings.

docs.title: 6. Select the Camera
docs.text:
By default, the software uses a local camera with camera ID 0.

If no image appears on the main screen:

  1. Open Settings → Camera.
  2. Keep Local camera selected.
  3. Set the camera ID to 0, click Save, and check the main screen.
  4. If there is still no image, try 1, 2, and 3 in order, saving after each change.

Signs of Success

The main screen continuously shows the camera view instead of a camera-unavailable or reconnecting message.

See Camera if multiple cameras are connected or you need a fallback camera.

docs.title: 7. Adjust the Patient and Camera Position
docs.text:
Adjust the camera or the patient's position until:

  • The patient faces the camera, with the full face and both eyes in view.
  • Hair, bedding, hands, or eyeglass frames do not cover the eyes.
  • Lighting is stable and the face is not too dark.
  • The patient can maintain the position naturally and comfortably.

If the main screen reports that no face is detected, facial landmarks cannot be located, or facial keypoints are invalid, see The Patient's Face or Eyes Are Not Detected.

docs.title: 8. Complete a Test Call
docs.text:
The current default sequence is:

Eyes open for 1.5 seconds → eyes closed for 1 second → eyes open for 1 second → eyes closed for 1.5 seconds.

During the test:

  1. Watch the progress bar at the top of the main screen.
  2. Hold each eye-open or eye-closed action until the current stage finishes.
  3. Start the next stage within 3 seconds of completing the previous one.
  4. After the whole sequence finishes, wait for the call alert and confirm that the ringtone can be heard.
  5. Click the red call alert button to stop the ringtone early.

Test Complete

Initial setup is successful when all of the following are true:

  • The camera view is continuous and clear.
  • The top progress bar advances with eye-open and eye-closed actions.
  • The call alert appears after the sequence finishes.
  • The ringtone can be heard through the computer or Bluetooth speaker.
  • Clicking the red call alert button stops the ringtone.

If progress does not move, repeatedly resets, or the alert cannot be heard, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Checks before daily use: Daily Use.
  • Adjust actions for the patient: Blink Pattern.
  • Adjust the ringtone and volume: Audio Alert.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This section helps family members or caregivers complete the initial setup and learn how to make daily calls.

docs.title: First-Time Setup
docs.text:
1. Download and extract the software to a fixed location.
  2. Open the software by double-clicking BlinkCall.exe.
  3. Download the model files under Settings → Blink Call → Download/Update model files.
  4. Check the camera view: allow camera access and make sure both of the patient's eyes are fully visible.
  5. Complete a test call: follow the top progress bar through the default blink sequence and confirm that the alert can be heard.

See First Use for the video, detailed steps, screenshots, and signs of successful setup.

docs.title: Daily Use
docs.text:
1. Open the software.
  2. Check that the camera view is continuous and clear.
  3. Make sure neither eye is covered.
  4. Complete the configured blink sequence.
  5. To stop the ringtone early, have a caregiver click the red call alert button.

See Daily Use for details.

docs.title: If Something Goes Wrong
docs.text:
• The software will not open or model files will not download.
  • There is no camera image, or no face is detected.
  • Blink progress does not move, calls do not trigger, or calls trigger accidentally.
  • A call is triggered but no alert can be heard.

For these problems, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Signs That Setup Is Complete
docs.text:
After the initial setup, all of the following should be true:

  • The main screen continuously shows the patient's camera view.
  • The top progress bar responds to eye-open and eye-closed actions.
  • The patient can complete the sequence without excessive fatigue.
  • The caregiver can hear the alert after the sequence finishes.
  • The caregiver can stop the alert and knows where to adjust the blink pattern, camera, and audio.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
After the first successful test call, you can adjust the software to suit the patient. Settings usually do not need frequent changes during daily use.

Open Settings at the top left of the main screen. After making changes, click Save.

Disclaimer

This tool is intended only to support caregiving and cannot replace human supervision. Do not reduce or omit necessary human supervision because you use this tool.

docs.title: What Would You Like to Adjust?
docs.text: What to adjust Page Suggestion The eye-open and eye-closed actions needed for a call Blink Pattern Test the defaults first, then make small changes The camera to use or a fallback camera Camera Keep Local camera selected for ordinary use Ringtone, volume, playback duration, and step prompts Audio Alert Preview the sounds and check the system volume Alerts when the camera image or face remains missing Audio Alert Set separate delays for the two conditions Language, theme, recording, logs, and restoring defaults Advanced Recording and logs are usually needed only for troubleshooting

docs.title: When Changing Settings
docs.text:
• Change one group of settings at a time, then save and complete a test call.
  • Choose blink actions the patient can complete reliably without excessive fatigue.
  • After changing the camera, return to the main screen and check for a continuous view with both eyes clearly visible.
  • After changing audio settings, check the software volume and the computer or Bluetooth speaker volume.
  • If settings have become confusing, use Settings → Others → Restore defaults, then test again.

docs.title: Changes Have Not Taken Effect
docs.text: Make sure you clicked Save at the bottom of the settings window. If the problem continues, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: When something goes wrong, check the camera view and messages on the main screen, then follow the relevant steps below.

docs.title: Start with These Checks
docs.text:
1. Make sure the software is fully extracted and is not running inside the compressed package.
  2. Make sure the model files have finished downloading.
  3. Check that the camera view is continuous and clear, with the patient's face and both eyes fully visible.
  4. Make sure Settings → Blink Call → Enable blink call is set to On.
  5. Make sure the computer or Bluetooth speaker is not muted.

If the problem continues, find the matching situation below.

docs.title: The Software Will Not Open
docs.text:
Check the following in order:

  1. Fully extract the downloaded software package.
  2. Open the extracted folder and double-click BlinkCall.exe.
  3. Keep BlinkCall.exe together with the other files in the folder. Do not move or copy the executable on its own.
  4. Download the package again, extract it to a new folder, and try again.

If the software still will not open, record the Windows version, software version, and any message on screen, then report the problem through GitHub Issues.

docs.title: Model Files Will Not Download
docs.text:
If you see “Network connection timed out,” “Network connection failed,” “Failed to request model information,” or “Failed to download model files”:

  1. Check that the computer can access the internet.
  2. Close the download message and reopen Settings → Blink Call.
  3. Click Download/Update again.
  4. Wait for the entire download to finish. Do not close the software during the download.

After a successful download, the progress window closes and the settings are saved automatically. The main screen should no longer show the message that model files are missing.

If repeated attempts fail, record the complete error message and report it through GitHub Issues.

docs.title: No Camera Image
docs.text:
If the main screen says the camera is not available:

  1. Make sure the camera is connected properly.
  2. Check that Windows allows desktop applications to access the camera.
  3. Close meeting, streaming, or camera applications that may be using the device.
  4. Open Settings → Camera and select Local camera.
  5. Start with camera ID 0. If no image appears, try 1, 2, and 3 in order.
  6. After each change, click Save and check the main screen.

If the main screen says “Camera connection was lost. Reconnecting...,” check the cable, reconnect the camera, and wait for automatic recovery.

If you use both a laptop's built-in camera and an external camera, you can configure a fallback camera. See Camera.

docs.title: The Patient's Face or Eyes Are Not Detected
docs.text:
The main screen may show:

  • “No face detected.”
  • “Failed to locate facial landmarks.”
  • “Invalid facial keypoints. Please check the patient's pose or eye occlusion.”

Adjust the camera or the patient's position:

  1. Have the patient face the camera.
  2. Keep the full face and both eyes in view, away from the edges of the image.
  3. Move hair, bedding, hands, or eyeglass frames away from the eyes.
  4. Improve lighting on the face. Avoid a dark face or strong backlighting.
  5. Keep the patient and camera steady and wait for recognition to recover.

docs.title: Blink Progress Does Not Move or Keeps Resetting
docs.text:
Check the following:

  1. Settings → Blink Call → Enable blink call is set to On.
  2. Show top progress bar on home page is set to Show.
  3. The patient's face and both eyes can be recognized continuously.
  4. Each eye-open or eye-closed action is held until the current stage is complete.
  5. The next stage starts within 3 seconds of finishing the previous one.
  6. The actions match Settings → Blink Call → Blink sequence.

Try restoring the default settings and testing the default sequence:

Eyes open for 1.5 seconds → eyes closed for 1 second → eyes open for 1 second → eyes closed for 1.5 seconds.

If the patient finds the current actions difficult, see Blink Pattern.

docs.title: The Sequence Finishes but No Call Is Triggered
docs.text:
1. Make sure the whole sequence finishes without the progress resetting midway.
  2. Make sure Enable blink call is set to On.
  3. Check that model files are not missing or damaged. You can check them again under Download/Update model files.
  4. Click Save, return to the main screen, and test again.

If the main screen reports an inference error or says blink detection is not working, close and reopen the software. If the problem continues, record the message and report it.

docs.title: Calls Are Triggered Accidentally
docs.text:
• Avoid using only a very short eye-closed action, which may be confused with a natural blink.
  • Increase the eye-closed duration slightly.
  • Add one or two action steps to make the complete sequence easier to distinguish from natural blinking.
  • Change one setting at a time and test several times after each change.
  • Consider the patient's stamina and avoid making the sequence too long.

See Blink Pattern for instructions.

docs.title: No Alert Sound
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Blink Call.
  2. Make sure Play call audio is set to On.
  3. Select a Call audio file and click Preview.
  4. Increase Audio volume in the software.
  5. Check the Windows volume and the speaker or Bluetooth speaker volume.
  6. If using a Bluetooth speaker, make sure the computer is still connected to the correct playback device.
  7. Save the settings and complete another test call.

If the preview works but a call produces no sound, check whether the blink sequence actually finished and the call alert appeared.

docs.title: Settings Have Become Confusing
docs.text:
Open Settings → Others → Restore defaults, confirm, and complete another test call.

Restoring defaults resets the blink pattern, camera, audio, and interface settings. It does not delete downloaded model files.

docs.title: Information to Include in a Report
docs.text:
When reporting a problem through GitHub Issues, include:

  • The Blink Call version.
  • The Windows version.
  • The actions taken before the problem occurred.
  • What you expected and what actually happened.
  • The complete message shown on the main screen.
  • Screenshots that help explain the problem.

If staff need logs or a camera recording, they will explain how to obtain them. Recordings may contain the patient's face and surroundings. Obtain consent first and do not upload sensitive footage directly to a public issue.
